title: bug: OAuth callback timeout is retained after the flow completes

triage_metadata.reasoning: The issue provides a clear, actionable bug report detailing a timer leak in the OAuth callback flow (packages/core/src/utils/oauth-flow.ts). It includes explicit steps to reproduce, root cause explanation, and expected behavior.
triage_metadata.effort_reasoning: The fix is restricted to packages/core/src/utils/oauth-flow.ts, where clearTimeout(timeoutId) needs to be called when the callback server closes or settles. Updating the cleanup in startCallbackServer and adding unit tests in oauth-flow.test.ts is straightforward and localized.

summary.problem: The OAuth callback server in startCallbackServer sets a 5-minute timeout timer, but does not clear it when the server closes after completion or error, leading to retained timers and memory/closure leaks.
summary.root_cause: In startCallbackServer() (packages/core/src/utils/oauth-flow.ts), timeoutId is set with setTimeout to abort the flow after 5 minutes. When server.close() is called (upon success, OAuth error, state mismatch, or general error), clearTimeout(timeoutId) is never called in the server 'close' event handler or cleanup phase.
summary.context: While timeoutId.unref() prevents Node process exit blocking, the timer reference and its associated closures remain in memory until 5 minutes expire, which can cause delayed execution of stale callbacks and memory leaks in long-running processes.

steps: In startCallbackServer in packages/core/src/utils/oauth-flow.ts, ensure clearTimeout(timeoutId) is called whenever the callback server closes or settles.
Add clearTimeout(timeoutId) inside the server.on('close', ...) listener (or central cleanup function) to clear the timeout when the server closes.

testing_strategy.expected_behavior: When startCallbackServer() completes (on success or error), clearTimeout is called so the 5-minute timeout timer does not remain active or fire after server closure.
verification_steps: In packages/core/src/utils/oauth-flow.test.ts, add a unit test using fake timers or spying on clearTimeout.
Verify that after sending a successful callback request to startCallbackServer(), clearTimeout is called or advancing fake time by 5 minutes does not trigger any stale rejection/abort.
